metadata.title: The role of teacher quality in fourth-grade mathematics instruction: evidence from TIMSS 2015

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The policy brief reports findings using TIMSS 2015 fourth-grade classroom data, but it does not provide methodological details on sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures. TIMSS is collected using a complex multistage design (students nested in classrooms/schools and sampled within countries), so analysts working with TIMSS microdata typically apply the provided student/sampling weights and, when available, replicate weights for correct standard errors. The brief does not specify whether the authors used these weights or relied on unweighted estimates, so the weighting approach cannot be verified from the provided text. For replication, users should consult the TIMSS 2015 technical documentation and the authors’ methods section (not included here) to confirm the exact weight variables and variance estimation method.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a policy brief summarizing relationships between teacher quality measures and instructional alignment/time, and the provided text does not describe PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes or any PV generation/combining procedure. Because the dependent variables emphasized here are instructional opportunity-to-learn constructs (alignment and instructional time) rather than PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable based on the information available. Missing-data handling is not reported in the excerpt, so the specific strategy (e.g., complete-case vs. imputation) cannot be determined from the provided material.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2015 fourth-grade classroom data across multiple countries, but the excerpt does not specify the analytic subsample definition (e.g., which teacher-quality measures, which classroom alignment/time indicators, or any exclusions).

data.outcome_summary: This IEA policy brief synthesizes evidence from TIMSS 2015 fourth-grade classroom data to address how teacher quality varies within and between countries and how teacher quality relates to instructional alignment and instructional time in mathematics. The brief reports that measures of teacher quality are only weakly related to one another, and that countries showing greater variation on one teacher-quality dimension (e.g., experience) also show greater variation on other dimensions (e.g., education/readiness to teach math topics). It further states that teacher-quality measures are not strong or consistent predictors of instructional alignment or instructional time, implying that teachers’ preparation may have limited influence on the classroom opportunity to learn as measured here. Finally, it highlights an equity pattern: disadvantaged students, in many countries, have higher-quality teachers by some measures. The excerpt does not provide model specifications, performance metrics, or PV/missing-data/weighting details, limiting methodological transparency.
